claim: Identical initial agents acquire held-out skill as a function of the feedback they receive: instructional (full) feedback > outcome-only (bandit) feedback > no feedback, and a non-learning persona shows no effect.
value: +0.3908 (95% CI [+0.3742, +0.4102], n=10 seeds) — primary contrast 'instruction_vs_no_feedback_developmental' (superiority): dev_full vs dev_none on final_heldout_accuracy: estimate +0.3908 (95% CI [+0.3742, +0.4102], n=10 seeds; relative +87.9%); threshold 0.0500 -> passed
limitations: Feedback conditions are properties of the synthetic environment; 'instruction' here means revealing the correct answer, not human teaching.
Retention measures forgetting dynamics built into each policy class (baselines do not forget by construction).
Simulated result from a synthetic world. Effects may simply reflect assumptions built into the simulator and are not estimates of real-world causal effects.

claim: In a society of developmental learners, giving every child aged 5-15 access to tutoring (extra instructional feedback episodes) raises held-out task accuracy at ages 16-20 relative to a cloned control society, and the effect appears only when agents can learn.
value: +0.0289 (95% CI [+0.0216, +0.0367], n=10 seeds) — primary contrast 'tutoring_effect_developmental' (superiority): dev_tutoring vs dev_control on cohort_accuracy_16_20: estimate +0.0289 (95% CI [+0.0216, +0.0367], n=10 seeds; relative +3.5%); threshold 0.0200 -> passed
limitations: Simulated effects reflect the simulator's assumption that tutoring = extra instructional-feedback episodes; they are not estimates of real tutoring effects.
Cohorts after year 0 include agents born during the run; births can differ between arms through downstream dynamics.
Depends on hpe.world semantics for tutoring_access and AgentState.tutored (sim/world lane).
Simulated result from a synthetic world. Effects may simply reflect assumptions built into the simulator and are not estimates of real-world causal effects.

claim: In a connected community, trust-weighted social learning diffuses skill so held-out accuracy (ages 10-60, year 15) exceeds an otherwise identical isolated community; seeded misinformation lowers accuracy, less so for a learner that discounts demonstrations conflicting with its own evidence.
value: -0.0040 (95% CI [-0.0074, -0.0002], n=10 seeds) — primary contrast 'connection_effect' (superiority): dev_connected vs dev_isolated on accuracy_10_60: estimate -0.0040 (95% CI [-0.0074, -0.0002], n=10 seeds; relative -0.5%); threshold — -> failed
limitations: Misinformation is a fictional-task construct (wrong demonstrations presented as correct); it says nothing about real-world misinformation.
Depends on hpe.world semantics for social_isolation and misinformation interventions.
Simulated result from a synthetic world. Effects may simply reflect assumptions built into the simulator and are not estimates of real-world causal effects.

claim: A learner with a shared representation trained on sort/compare/signal adapts faster to the never-practised 'barter' family than independently trained specialists when barter shares the latent structure, and shows no benefit (or negative transfer) when it does not.
value: +0.0895 (95% CI [+0.0503, +0.1228], n=10 seeds) — primary contrast 'shared_representation_vs_specialists' (superiority): developmental vs developmental_specialists on transfer_auc/shared/trained: estimate +0.0895 (95% CI [+0.0503, +0.1228], n=10 seeds; relative +13.7%); threshold 0.0300 -> passed
limitations: Barter is never practised during development; leakage/holdout_symbols_in_practice must be 0.
Because all rules are linear in the raw features, a shared representation can only help through sample efficiency.
Simulated result from a synthetic world. Effects may simply reflect assumptions built into the simulator and are not estimates of real-world causal effects.

claim: Held-out skill comes from experience-driven parameter learning, not from scripted age gates: freezing policy learning or withholding feedback removes the gain; other components contribute measurably or not at all.
value: +0.4086 (95% CI [+0.3947, +0.4255], n=10 seeds) — primary contrast 'learning_is_necessary' (superiority): developmental vs ablate_learning on final_heldout_accuracy: estimate +0.4086 (95% CI [+0.3947, +0.4255], n=10 seeds; relative +91.9%); threshold 0.1000 -> passed
limitations: Curriculum only affects self-directed practice choice; in this fixed-schedule lab it may have no effect by design.
Ablation flags are implemented by the research/development lane; this experiment only toggles them.

claim: Agents whose policy develops from experience (developmental learner) reach higher accuracy on held-out symbols (never seen in practice) than equally-resourced static-persona, memory-only, or plain-RL agents given an identical item and feedback stream.
value: +0.0121 (95% CI [-0.0080, +0.0306], n=10 seeds) — primary contrast 'developmental_vs_strongest_baseline' (superiority): developmental vs plain_rl on final_heldout_accuracy: estimate +0.0121 (95% CI [-0.0080, +0.0306], n=10 seeds; relative +1.4%); threshold 0.0837 -> failed; control = strongest of memory_only=0.7727, plain_rl=0.8369, static_persona=0.4381 -> plain_rl
limitations: Synthetic task world; held-out = unseen symbols under the same hidden rules, not unseen humans.
Baseline hyperparameters (plain_rl lr=0.05) were tuned on task seeds 1001-1003, never on evaluation seeds 0-9.
The developmental learner's hyperparameters are owned by the research/development lane; if they were tuned on evaluation seeds this result is optimistic.
Age gate (perceptual feature access) is a scripted assumption applied identically to all arms; the no_age_gate sensitivity variant removes it.
Simulated result from a synthetic world. Effects may simply reflect assumptions built into the simulator and are not estimates of real-world causal effects.

claim: A developmental learner (Tier-2 policy, hpe.development) predicts held-out human choices in multiple-cue probability learning better than the strongest non-developmental model, including static models fitted to other participants and the memory-only / plain-RL baselines.
value: -0.1101 (95% CI [-0.1395, -0.0827], n=153 participants) — Primary contrast developmental - ref_instance_based on held-out MCPL participants: +0.2289 nats/choice (95% CI [+0.1708, +0.2890], n=69); minimum effect of interest 0.02 nats/choice; rule: passed if ci_high < 0 and estimate <= -0.02; failed if ci_low > -0.02; inconclusive otherwise, or if the developmental class is not available in the build.
limitations: Teacher-forced one-step-ahead likelihood measures predictive fit to human choice sequences, not generative realism.
Registry classes are not tuned beyond lapse/reward scale; reference cognitive models get small grids. This favours the reference models.
Participants are adults in short laboratory tasks; this says nothing about life-course development or the simulator's world.
Psych-101 transcripts were used to train the Centaur language model; irrelevant here because no language model is used, noted for context.
MCPL cue encoding (one-hot + scalar, 12 features) is a modelling choice shared by all models.

claim: A centred least-squares estimate of the causal excursion effect of delivering an activity suggestion (vs none) on log 30-minute step count, computed from the public HeartSteps V1 data, is consistent with the effect published by Klasnja et al. (2019).
value: +0.1154 (95% CI [-0.0046, +0.2423], n=37 participants) — any_suggestion: estimate +12.2% (95% cluster bootstrap CI [-0.5%, +27.4%]); published +14% (p = .06) lies inside the CI. Rule: consistent if log(1 + published_percent/100) lies inside our 95% cluster-bootstrap CI for the corresponding term; the primary comparison is any_suggestion.
limitations: The public dataset contains 37 participants; the paper reports a 6-week MRT with 44 adults. The analysed samples may differ.
The paper's exact control covariates and outcome transform are not verified from its full text in this session (only the abstract was accessible).
This is the only real causal estimate in the repository. It is not mixed with, and does not validate, any simulation result.
